It schedules sleep and cooling, sets effort caps of 3-4/10 on easy days, runs in the cooler hours and puts a heart-rate cap on the long run. The plan totals 29 mi (5+6+4+4+10), which is well under the 36 mi she planned and the 35 mi peak. The 10 mi long run is moderate, so there is no sharp jump in volume or long run, and I don't rate it unsafe. It is still only a hold: 29 mi is slightly above the 27 mi she actually ran, not a real back-off. It also keeps a threshold session (2 x 10 min at 7/10) for someone who says she is 'tired all the time' and 'drained'. A better reply would drop the quality day or make it optional, with a fallback, since she is run down. The draft also cites heat, a hot apartment, 5.5-hour nights and mid-August knee trouble. None of this appears on the card, which says 'Knee is fine', so these details can't be checked and may be invented. The days are clear enough to run. Overall it's sound but cautious only up to a point. The answer to her question is good. Keeping the threshold session and the flat volume hold back the score.
